_meta.source: IEC 60364-5-52:2009 Table B.52.4 (PVC insulated copper, two loaded conductors, 30 C ambient): columns B1 (insulated conductors in conduit on or in a masonry wall; NOT A1, conduit in a thermally insulated wall, which is rated lower) and C (clipped direct). The 1 mm2 row is not in Table B.52.4 (it starts at 1.5 mm2); its values are the same-basis BS 7671 Table 4D1A figures (methods B and C). Pakistani n/d sizes converted with formulas.md section W (A = n x pi x (d x 25.4 / 2)^2) and rated as the IEC size they are sold as when their real area is at least 90% of it, else the next smaller IEC size (conservative).
_meta.status: Engineer to confirm against the IEC table and Pakistan Cables / Fast Cables datasheets before launch. Ratings are for single-phase or three-phase circuits of one cable in free air or conduit at 30 C; grouping and hot roof spaces need derating by an electrician.
_meta.fields: cables: area_mm2 nominal conductor size; ampacity_a per installation method. pk_sizes: strands, strand diameter in inches, real area, rated_as_mm2 = the row of cables used for its ampacity. breaker_margin_load_types: load types whose MCB is chosen at I_b x margin (continuous motor-type loads), so a 1.5 ton AC gets a 16 A MCB on 2.5 mm2 rather than 10 A on 1 mm2.

methods.B1: In conduit in a brick or plastered (masonry) wall, most Pakistani house wiring; a conduit buried in thermal insulation is method A1 and is rated lower
methods.C: Clipped direct to a wall or surface

mcb_curves._source: IEC 60898-1 instantaneous tripping ranges: B 3-5 x In, C 5-10 x In, D 10-20 x In

B.use: lighting, sockets and resistive loads (heaters, irons, geysers)

C.use: air conditioners, fridges, motors, water pumps and mixed socket circuits

D.use: transformers, welding machines and large motors with heavy inrush

min_area_mm2._source: IEC 60364-5-52 Table 52.2 minimum conductor sizes and common Pakistani practice (3/29 for lighting points, 7/29 for sockets and air conditioners); engineer to confirm
